One attacker broke into the dormant Obama White House account and made pro-Iran…

De Beers Group and GIA (Gemological Institute of America) have acquired a 30% shareholding in Tracr, the De Beers Group-backed company behind the development of the pioneering diamond provenance blockchain-driven platform. The agreement marks a significant milestone in Tracr’s evolution towards independence and reflects GIA’s confidence in the platform’s role as an industry-wide infrastructure to […]

top.aiSummary: De Beers Group and GIA have acquired a combined 30% stake in Tracr, the blockchain-driven diamond provenance platform.

da.title: De Beers og GIA køber andel i diamantverifikationsplatform
da.summary: De Beers Group og Gemological Institute of America (GIA) har hver erhvervet en 30% andel i Tracr, en blockchain-baseret diamantoprindelsesplatform støttet af De Beers, hvilket markerer et vigtigt skridt mod platformens uafhængighed og brancheomfattende adoption.

es.title: De Beers y GIA adquieren participación en plataforma de verificación de diamantes
es.summary: De Beers Group y el Gemological Institute of America (GIA) han adquirido cada uno una participación del 30% en Tracr, una plataforma de procedencia de diamantes basada en blockchain respaldada por De Beers, marcando un paso clave hacia la independencia de la plataforma y su adopción en toda la industria.

top.title: Australian jewellery retailer confirms cyber attack
top.snippet: An Australian jewellery business has confirmed a cyber incident after hackers claimed they accessed the company's systems and stole more than half a terabyte of data.

editorialTake:
Anthropic’s IPO filing signals a pivotal moment in AI’s commercialization race. Daniela Amodei’s confidence in delivering returns despite skepticism highlights a growing divide between AI hype and tangible business models. This isn’t just another tech debut; it’s a test of whether AI companies can justify sky-high valuations with real revenue streams. Investors will want to see if Anthropic’s approach to safety and proprietary models can translate into sustainable profits or if it’s just another AI bubble waiting to burst.

Meanwhile, Meta’s launch of Hatch, a $200-a-month AI agent, exposes a sharp tension in AI’s monetization strategy. Charging a premium for AI tools aimed at everyday tasks risks alienating users accustomed to free or low-cost alternatives. Meta’s recent AI-related security breach only deepens the question: can big tech balance aggressive AI monetization with the trust and safety users demand? The real test is whether customers will pay for AI convenience or recoil from the risks and costs.
oneSentenceSummary: Retailers’ use of AI to chase both mass efficiency and bespoke luxury experiences upends the assumption that scale and exclusivity cannot coexist digitally.
